doc.title: Peter Ecklund interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: His cornet and ending a tune on a high note
summary: Ecklund explains why he plays a cornet in small groups, its mellower sound and better low notes, and the high-note ending trick on 'I'm in the Mood for Love'.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Well this, actually it was made maybe 75 miles from here in Fullerton. And I think it’s a copy of an old instrument, I really don’t know what. I’ve tried to get the guy who built it on the phone but I haven’t succeeded. But basically the reason I play this, in small groups it’s got, I’ve always played trumpet in big bands, but this, the low notes come out better. And it has I think a more interesting sound as a solo voice. I mean there’s not a big difference between cornet and trumpet and you can get trumpets that sound like cornets and cornets that sound like trumpets. But in general it’s a bit mellower, and there is more variety in sound that you can get out of it, between the mellowest and the brightest sound. So you can be a little bit, sort of more vocal on it. It’s not a huge difference. It’s not as easy to play the high notes, but the low notes sound better.

As a matter of fact you mentioned playing a high note, I noticed on one of the tunes I just heard you play down there, I think it was “I’m in the Mood for Love,” and they got to the end of that and you were playing the melody in the lead, and it ended up on a pretty high note.

Well that’s sort of a standard, I mean you could say it’s a cheap trick but it generally works, particularly in a kind of semi-chaotic situation like that. If you can find a good © Fiillius Jazz Archive -2-
sounding high note and hold it at the end then it kind of doesn’t matter what happens, it kind of covers over everything.
It attracts attention. Yeah, and as you said it was semi-chaotic, as the band kind of found the end there, I wondered how long they were going to keep you hanging up there.
Well I took a good breath before I started, I knew it was going to be a while.
